page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-96 is a compute-focused virtual server based on the x86_64 architecture and powered by Intel Xeon processors running at 2.6 GHz. The instance provisions 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory is configured at 96 GB, establishing an exact 1 GB of RAM per vCPU allocation. The hardware cache hierarchy features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 54 MB of unified L3 cache. Supported CPU extensions include AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance contains zero bundled local storage devices, zero GPUs, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external block storage and network provisioning.

Benchmark results demonstrate distinct separation between single-thread execution and highly parallel multi-threaded throughput. The instance achieves top-quartile multi-core metrics, registering 90557.44 in stress-ng multi-core and 15886.0 in Geekbench multi-core assessments. Software compilation via Clang reaches 49061.0, and ray tracing scores hit 80320.0, both residing in the top twenty-five percent. Memory bandwidth under cached 16 KB read blocks reaches 4889.85 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measures 60.55 GB/sec alongside 87.58 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-core benchmarks perform in the median tier, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1843.49 and Geekbench single-core at 1475.0.

The 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-dense applications by avoiding expenditures on unutilized RAM. However, the constrained memory footprint presents a functional tradeoff for datasets requiring extensive resident memory. Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-96 is technically aligned with parallel computing workloads, software build grids, batch data processing, ray tracing, and static web serving.
